what: R14: benign failure rates per hour and per day for every real-deployment run with a benign floor, per-run counts and settings, a block bootstrap over consecutive untouched one-second segments, and the pooled floor decomposed so that no pool mixes schemes
answers: R3 W3: 'Report benign rates per hour or day, with per-run counts and a block bootstrap'
R3 W3: 'The 13/4,733 pool mixes schemes and authentication settings across nine runs'

definitions.untouched_segment: an anchored one-second segment that holds no row any trial wrote, edited or named (the paper's counting rule; reproduce/verify_all.py touched_segments and, for E7/E8, e7_verify's benign floor with the trials' deleted events)
definitions.k: untouched one-second segments that fail verification (the benign floor's numerator)
definitions.per_untouched_hour: k / n x 3600: failures per hour of untouched anchored seconds (seconds that held rows, were sealed and were not touched by a trial)
definitions.per_wallclock_hour: k / window duration x 3600: failures per hour of the run window
definitions.exact_interval: Clopper-Pearson 95% interval of k/n (exp/rig/stats.py), scaled like the rate

block_bootstrap.method: circular block bootstrap over the run's untouched one-second segments in time order; replicate statistic = failure proportion; percentile interval
block_bootstrap.block_length_unit: consecutive untouched one-second segments (each a distinct second; L = 60 spans at least 60 s of wall-clock time, i.e. at least twelve 5 s monitor polls)
block_bootstrap.rng: numpy PCG64, SeedSequence([seed, run index in FLOOR_RUNS, L])
block_bootstrap.pools: stratified by run (blocks never cross runs)
block_bootstrap.k_zero: degenerate (every replicate is 0); exact interval reported instead
